title: Blood Lactate Measurements and Analysis during Exercise: A Guide for Clinicians
publisher: Journal of Diabetes Science and Technology
claims: MLSS is defined as the highest intensity at which blood lactate increases by no more than 1 mmol/L during the last 20 minutes of a 30-minute constant work rate test.
Reported blood lactate concentrations at MLSS range from about 1.5 mmol/L to almost 7 mmol/L, with an average of approximately 3.7 mmol/L.
An individual's MLSS and lactate threshold occur at different work rates, although the two values are correlated.
